Hey guys

For my weekly indie-game preview show I recently had a look at rebuild 3: Gangs of Deadsville, a post apocalyptic zombie survival ame where you need to rebuild civilization after a terrible zombie infestation.

Rebuild 3: Gangs of Deadsville is a strategy sim game with a good helping of narrative and dark humor. It's a thoughtful game that'll make you fond of your survivors before you send them to their deaths for the greater good. As you expand your fort to new buildings, you'll decide between farms or fortifications, housing or hospitals, and make tough decisions to fend off raiders, illness, starvation, and madness. And the dead are still out there wandering the streets, hungrier than ever.

Here is the first game. http://armorgames.com/play/10572/rebuild It all started with a flash game of tactical zombie survival; kinda similar to This War of Mine. Totally worth it. I didn't enjoy too much the second part; nevertheless I'm looking forward to test this third one.

What are you suggesting I do by comparing it to "my bank"?

Voat has solid encryption, many banks have not. However banks usually get the "EV" certificate for money, which gives a green navigation bar and makes them look more safe but actually means they pay some money for it as proof they are who they claim to be.

Edit:

Some banks do this to support outdated (i.e. Win XP) clients and don't enforce strong encryption.

There are two things, one is how strong the website has profen it is run by who it says it is. This Can get you a green bar.

The other thing is how safe the encryption is, it can be unsafe with green bar or very safe with a security warning.

Voat's not vulnerable to heartbleed because it doesn't use OpenSSL, the SSL implementation that had the heartbleed vulnerability. It's written in .NET, which has its own SSL implementation independent of OpenSSL - but thanks for checking!
